name: חֲזָהאֵל
summary: Hazael, king of Aram at Damascus. Yahweh told Elijah at Horeb to anoint him king over Aram (1Ki 19:15–17); Elisha wept before him, saying “Yahweh has made me see you king over Aram”, and foretold the evil he would do to Israel; the next day he smothered Ben-hadad and reigned in his place (2Ki 8:7–15). He fought Joram and Ahaziah at Ramoth-gilead (2Ki 8:28–29), and in the days of Jehu “Yahweh began to cut off Israel, and Hazael struck them in all the borders of Israel” (2Ki 10:32); he took Gath and turned toward Jerusalem until Joash paid him off (2Ki 12:18–19), and Amos foretold fire on “the house of Hazael” (Amo 1:4). The name is the verb חָזָה “he has seen” with אֵל “God”; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Go … and anoint חֲזָאֵל king over Aram.”
“Yahweh has made me see you king over Aram.”
He spread a wet cloth over Ben-hadad's face, “and Hazael reigned in his place”.
“Yahweh began to cut off Israel; and Hazael struck them in all the borders of Israel.”
He took Gath and set his face to go up against Jerusalem.
Yahweh gave Israel into the hand of Hazael all his days.
“I will send a fire into the house of Hazael.”
חָזָה “he saw”, the verb of the name's first part.

note: Takes h.bp.ai (23 tokens, spellings חֲזָהאֵל and חֲזָאֵל); h.bo.ai is a zero-token cross-reference. Hazael was an Aramean, and the name is as much Aramaic (ḥzy “see”, Jastrow) as Hebrew. Assyrian annals of Shalmaneser III name him (Ḫaza-ilu); not followed to an edition.
